📜 Open-Source Commercial Licensing Breakdown (MIT vs. Apache 2.0 vs. Meta Llama):

Choosing the right open-weights license is critical for enterprise legal compliance:

  • MIT License (DeepSeek R1, DeepSeek V3, Mistral NeMo):
    • Terms: Maximum freedom. Royalty-free commercial use, modification, closed-source distribution, and private internal deployment.
    • Ceiling: Zero user caps or revenue ceilings. Complete enterprise peace of mind.
  • Apache 2.0 License (Qwen 2.5 series, Granite 3.0):
    • Terms: Enterprise-standard open license with explicit patent protection and grant. Free commercial use and modification.
    • Ceiling: No user or monthly active user (MAU) restrictions.
  • Meta Llama 3.3 Community License:
    • Terms: Free for research and commercial use for 99% of businesses.
    • Enterprise Clause: If your product or service reaches >700 million Monthly Active Users (MAU) in the previous calendar month, you must request an explicit commercial license from Meta.
    • Training Restriction: Prohibits using Llama outputs to improve or train other non-Llama models.
💡 Enterprise Verdict: DeepSeek R1 (MIT) and Qwen 2.5 (Apache 2.0) carry zero MAU ceiling risk, whereas Meta Llama requires compliance sign-off for consumer internet scale.

advisorResponses.query: How does KV cache overhead affect VRAM when running 128k context locally?
advisorResponses.preview: 🧠 KV Cache Memory Overhead & Long-Context Sizing: When running long-context models locally, the KV (Key-Value) Cache often consumes as much VRAM as the model weights themselve...
advisorResponses.fullResp:
🧠 KV Cache Memory Overhead & Long-Context Sizing:

When running long-context models locally, the KV (Key-Value) Cache often consumes as much VRAM as the model weights themselves:

  • The KV Cache Formula:
    KV Cache (Bytes) = 2 × Layers × KV_Heads × Head_Dim × Bytes_per_Element × Context_Length × Batch_Size
  • Memory Impact at 128k Context:
    • At 8k context, a 70B model requires only ~1.5GB for KV cache.
    • At 128k context in standard FP16, the KV cache requires ~24GB to 32GB of VRAM solely for attention context!
  • Key Optimizations to Fit 128k Context:
    1. FP8 / INT4 KV Cache: Quantizing the KV cache (--cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 in llama.cpp or kv_cache_dtype="fp8" in vLLM) cuts memory usage by 50%–75% with near-zero perplexity loss.
    2. Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): Modern architectures like Llama 3.3 70B and Qwen 2.5 use 8 KV heads instead of 64, reducing KV cache size by 8x out of the box.
💡 Practical Homelab Sizing: On a 64GB Mac Studio or dual RTX 3090 (48GB), run Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B (Q4 ~20GB) with FP8 KV cache to comfortably support full 32k–64k context windows.
